messages:
ravi (Contractor): Quick question — I'm part-time (0.6 FTE) and based in Berlin. Our team has a mandatory office week that hits the UK/US year-end blackout. How are accruals handled for part-timers during blackout?

maria (People Ops): Hi Ravi — welcome Q. For part-time employees we prorate accruals by FTE. Company blackout days are treated as paid company holidays for employees on active contracts on those dates. For contractors we treat it case-by-case.

ravi (Contractor): So if I'm 0.6 FTE and the blackout is 5 working days, do I get 3 days (0.6 * 5) as paid holiday, or is it 5 days pro-rated differently because of local law?

sandra (EMEA HR): Great point. Local labor law can change things. In Germany, a public/company holiday is generally full-day paid if it falls on a scheduled working day. We calculate the holiday pro-rata based on scheduled working days per week, not calendar days.

maria (People Ops): TL;DR: We'll convert blackout to paid days equal to your scheduled workdays during the blackout period. If your regular schedule only includes 3 of the 5 blackout weekdays, you get 3 paid days. For contractors we need the SOW to confirm.

ravi (Contractor): My SOW lists 3 days/week. So sounds like I'll get 3 days paid. Any impact to accrual banks?

ben (Payroll): Payroll note: company-paid blackout days do not debit PTO/sick banks. However, if a contractor is not on an active SOW covering those dates, payroll will default to 'unpaid' and charge no accruals. We need a signed SOW or contract amendment by payroll cutoff.

ravi (Contractor): Got it. How about swapping the blackout day to another day (my manager suggested a swap) — is that allowed for part-timers?

maria (People Ops): We allow one-for-one day swaps with manager approval and People Ops sign-off. Manager must confirm coverage and the swap must not increase weekly hours beyond permitted FTE. Fill out the "Holiday Swap" form on the intranet.

sandra (EMEA HR): Note: If the swap creates overtime under local law, we can't approve it.

hr-bot: Reminder: send contract/SOW updates to payroll at least 6 business days before period end to avoid miscoding. https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/contractors :spiral_calendar:

ravi (Contractor): Thanks everyone — I'll ask my manager to submit the swap + attach my SOW.

maria (People Ops): Happy to help. If you want, DM me the SOW and I can fast-track review. :thumbsup:
